get.description: Lists humans on this instance, ascending by id. `?type=` narrows to one registration type; `?id=a,b,c` fetches a specific set in one request (unknown ids are omitted, not an error). Combining them intersects. Returns a summary per human — use GET /v2/humans/{id} for the full resource.

parameters.description: Filter to one registration type, e.g. webhook or discord:user. Omit for every type.
parameters.name: type

schema.description: Filter to one registration type, e.g. webhook or discord:user. Omit for every type.

parameters.description: Comma-separated ids to fetch, e.g. id=123,456 — the same form as the bulk tracking delete's uid=. Unknown ids are omitted rather than erroring. Omit to list everything.
parameters.name: id

schema.description: Comma-separated ids to fetch, e.g. id=123,456 — the same form as the bulk tracking delete's uid=. Unknown ids are omitted rather than erroring. Omit to list everything.

delete.description: Removes the human along with every tracking rule, profile and summary schedule they own. Irreversible. 404 if the human does not exist. Triggers a state reload.
delete.summary: Delete a human and all their data

get.description: Returns the full human resource. blocked_alerts is a read-only derived field. 404 if the human does not exist.

Returns every profile for the human (profile_no, name, area, location, active_hours). active_hours is a typed JSON array of schedule entries ([] when no schedule is set). 404 if the human does not exist.

areas.description: Requested area names. Matched case-insensitively against the fences this human may select; duplicates are collapsed and anything unmatched comes back in the rejected list rather than being dropped silently.

trusted.description: Set true to select fences that are not userSelectable — for a server-side client that has already authorised the change (e.g. the user drew the fence). Honoured because the caller holds the API secret. Unknown fence names are still rejected.

active_hours.description: New active-hours schedule ([] clears it, omitted leaves it unchanged). Validated against the strict schema.

name.description: New profile name. Omit to leave it unchanged.

boss.description: Catch-all for boss encounters: set true to match only boss invasions (stored grunt_type "boss"). One-of mode field. Mutually exclusive with the others; gender not allowed.

clean.description: Auto-delete the alert on expiry (clean bitmask bit 1). Omit to disable (default false). Returned as null when false.

distance.description: Radius in metres around the anchor location. Omit (or 0) to match by the profile's geofence areas instead of a radius — 0 means area-based, NOT zero metres (stored as 0). Returned as null when at its wildcard.

edit.description: Keep the message updated in place (clean bitmask bit 2). Omit to disable (default false). Returned as null when false.

everything.description: Catch-all wildcard: set true to match EVERY invasion (stored grunt_type "everything"). Equivalent to omitting every mode field, which is the wildcard; set it explicitly when you want the intent on the wire. Mutually exclusive with the others; gender not allowed.

gender.description: Grunt gender filter: any|male|female. Omit to match any gender (defaults to 'any', stored as 0). ONLY valid together with type_id. Returned as null when 'any' (or when not in type_id mode).

grunt_id.description: Game-master grunt id; resolves to that grunt's name and implies its own gender. One-of mode field. Mutually exclusive with the others; gender not allowed. Read-back reports the rule as grunt_type, because that is what is stored — see grunt_type.

grunt_type.description: The stored targeting value, and the ONE targeting field every read emits. Accepts any grunt name the bot accepts: a pokemon type ("water"), a named grunt ("giovanni", "blanche", "mixed", "npc_0"), or a catch-all ("everything", "boss"). type_id and grunt_id are input conveniences that resolve to one of these. Pokestop-event names are not valid here — use /incident. Enumerate valid names from GET /api/masterdata/grunts. One-of mode field; may be combined with gender.

override_areas.description: Restrict this rule to these geofence areas (mutually exclusive with distance > 0 and override_location_label). Omit for none. Returned as null when unset.

override_location_label.description: Saved-location label to use instead of the profile location (requires distance > 0; mutually exclusive with override_areas). Omit for none. Returned as null when unset.

summary.description: Route into the summary digest (clean bitmask bit 4). Omit to disable (default false). Returned as null when false.

template.description: DTS template name. Omit (or empty) to use the server's configured default template (stored as ""). Returned as null when at its wildcard.

type_id.description: Pokemon type id (1-18); grunt_type resolves to that type's lowercased name. At most one mode field may be set — this OR grunt_id OR grunt_type OR everything OR boss. Omitting all of them matches EVERY invasion (stored "everything") — blank is the wildcard, as elsewhere in v2. In responses, the active mode field is always present; the other mode fields are omitted/null.

profile.description: The created profile. Omitted only when the post-insert read-back failed; profile_no is still authoritative.

profile_no.description: The profile_no assigned to the new profile — the LOWEST FREE number, which the caller cannot predict
